node.label: Daniel K Richter
node.date_label: “War and Culture: The Iroquois Experience” (1983) · The Ordeal of the Longhouse (1992) · Facing East from Indian Country (2001)
node.description: A historian of early North America who reconstructs colonial encounters from the standpoint of Native communities. In a Penn interview report he explains his decision to unsettle narratives organized around westward European settlement. His method also acknowledges the limits of reconstruction: Michael Monescalchi’s substantive reading of the Facing East prologue emphasizes contextual inference without pretending to recover another person’s vision transparently. Indigenous history here names the subject and method; it supplies no inference about the historian’s own identity.
